guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / flail chest and rib fractures
title: Flail chest injury during a rugby match
setting: Rugby tournament. Player tackled, fell under ruck, did not get up. Extreme right-sided chest pain, breathlessness, visible paradoxical movement on right side.
verdictExplanation: Severe flail chest with paradoxical chest wall movement, extreme pain, dyspnea, and borderline low BP (90/52). Sick: call 999 immediately and manage.

er.acvpu: Alert but in Pain (moving to unresponsive)

shared.response: Alert but in pain, becoming unresponsive
shared.breathing: Laboured, rapid and shallow; paradoxical chest movement

history.complaint: Severe pain in right side, chest injury
history.history: Tackled by two players, fell under the ensuing ruck 5 minutes ago
history.injuries: Suspect multiple rib fractures and flail chest on the right side
history.additional: Player becomes extremely distressed if allowed to view the injury

followUp.question: What is the correct first aid management for a flail chest injury?

options.text: Call 999, support the patient in a semi-sitting position, leaning towards the injured side, and hold arm on injured side in a sling
Bind the chest tightly with heavy elastic bandages to stop paradoxical movement
Lie him flat on his back and tell him to hold his breath
Perform chest compressions immediately to keep the lungs inflated

followUp.explanation: Flail chest requires an immediate 999 call. Support the patient in a semi-sitting position, leaning *towards* the injured side to maximize expansion of the uninjured lung. Hold the arm on the injured side in a sling to support the chest wall. Never bind the chest tightly as it restricts ventilation.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Call 999. Support in semi-sitting position leaning to injured side, apply sling. Reassure.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected flail chest / multiple rib fractures. Give high-flow oxygen. Monitor SpO₂ and BP. If he goes unresponsive, safely log-roll to recovery position on the *injured* side to protect the uninjured lung.
